text: Everything built in this course so far has almost certainly been built directly in one org. A real application doesn't ship that way — it moves through a chain of environments, tested at each stage, before it ever touches the data people's jobs depend on.

Four sandbox types, in order of weight. Developer: metadata only, for one person's active work. Developer Pro: the same, with more storage. Partial Copy: metadata plus a sampled slice of real data, for realistic QA. Full: a complete copy of metadata and data, for staging and final user acceptance testing before production.

A change set moves metadata — objects, fields, rules, flows, layouts — between two connected orgs. Never business data, only configuration. You create an outbound change set in the source org, add components and their dependencies, upload it. In the target org, it shows up as an inbound change set, where you validate as a dry run, then deploy. Once uploaded, it's closed — to resend updated components, you clone it.

Change sets only move between orgs that are already connected — no version control, no diff, no rollback history beyond what Setup shows. Teams that need source control, code review, or a CI/CD pipeline move to Salesforce CLI with the Metadata API instead, deploying from a version-controlled project. Same components, moved by a repeatable, scriptable process.

A few non-negotiables. Validate before deploying to production, and actually read the warnings, not just the errors. Deploy during low-usage windows, since some deployments can briefly affect performance. Keep an environment strategy on paper, so where a change goes next is never a guess. And never test or demo directly in production.

Sandboxes for building and testing, change sets or CLI for moving metadata between them, validation before every production deploy. Next: making sure the people who actually use this app, use it well.
